title: 第 1章 我出家了第2 章 出家之后的第一晚
slug: 杀妖涨修为道爷我成了
lines: “此物......倒是别致。”
老道士饶有兴致地打量着手里的“打火机”，指尖抚上金属防火罩，微微发力。
沈回蹲在火坑旁，欲言又止，可最后只是沉默地咽了口唾沫。
这打火机是他上周从烧烤摊顺来的，当时还得意占了老板三块钱的便宜，现在却悔得肠子发青，恨不得再穿越回去抽自己两巴掌。
早知道有此一劫，他说什么也要弄把军刀，再不济也要将《黄庭》诸经誊抄几卷，说不定还能忽悠忽悠眼前的人。
“此物当真能引地火？”老道士身侧的年轻徒弟好奇发问。
沈回含糊应了一声。
老道则将斑白的眉毛拧成疙瘩，手上力道再加三分。
金属防火罩顿时“嘎吱”作响。
“哎～道长且慢！”
沈回一个箭步上前，伸手拿回打火机，生怕对方将其给捏爆了。
“不是这般使的。”
他拇指一按，“咔哒”一声轻响，一簇橘火便窜了起来。
“瞧，这样。”
道士盯着那火，半晌不语。
年轻徒弟也凑近了些，憨厚的面上满是讶色：“真是奇怪，竟不含半点灵力波动！”
沈回将打火机递过去，顺手抄起脚边的枯枝，拨了拨火堆里埋着的红薯。
焦香混着炭气散开，破庙里终于有了些暖意。
他又开始庆幸当初顺手牵羊的是打火机而不是餐巾纸了，至少现在还能混口热的吃食不是？
清瘦老道从徒弟手里接过打火机，左右翻看，指尖泛起一层莹莹青光：
“内有一丝天雷余韵，外接些许地煞精气......”
他突然眯起眼睛，“小哥，此物从何而来？”
“祖传的小把戏。”
沈回面不改色，从火堆里扒拉出两个不大的红薯，同时心中暗自鄙夷。
什么劳什子天雷余韵，地煞精气，不过就是打火机里面的压电陶瓷和液态丁烷。
作为一个三天没吃上热食的穿越者，他此时只惦记着手里的红薯，哪有闲心扯这些玄虚。
至于眼前这两个不知所谓的道士......别说只是想看看他的打火机，便是要将他当做妖邪打杀了，也得先等他填饱肚子再说。
沈回用袖子垫着手拿起一个红薯，左右手倒腾着吹了口气，十指飞快地揭开那层焦皮。
皮上沾着些炭灰，他没扔，一并塞进嘴里，嚼得还挺仔细。
红薯不大，三两口便被他吃了个精光。
将最后一口红薯咽了，沈回又趁机瞥了两人一眼。
只见老道士面容清瘦，一身灰布道袍洗得发白，背上缚着一只细长木匣，以布带裹了。
年轻徒弟则脸膛黝黑，背着口半人高的藤箱，箱角挂个铃铛，另有个红得扎眼的葫芦。
啧！
这卖相不咋地啊！
沈回嘬了嘬牙花子，心说这俩人言语间倒是有几分高人气度，可这身打扮嘛……
怎么说呢，相貌的确是有那么几分仙气，但你见过穿草鞋的高人吗？还是在这么冷的天！
content_en:
"This thing... is quite unique."
The old Taoist priest looked at the "lighter" in his hand with great interest, touched the metal fireproof cover with his fingertips, and exerted slight pressure.
Shen Hui squatted by the fire pit and hesitated to speak, but in the end he just swallowed in silence.
He got this lighter from the barbecue stall last week. At that time, he was proud to take advantage of the boss's three yuan, but now he regrets it so much that he wishes he could go back in time and slap himself twice.
If he had known about this disaster, he would have gotten a saber no matter what. Even if it didn't work, he would have copied several volumes of the "Huang Ting" scriptures, and maybe he could fool the people in front of him.
"Can this thing really ignite the earth's fire?" The young apprentice beside the old Taoist priest asked curiously.
Shen Hui responded vaguely.
The old Taoist twisted his gray eyebrows into knots and added another three points of strength to his hands.
The metal fire cover suddenly "creaked".
"Hey~ Wait a minute!"
Shen Hui stepped forward and reached out to take back the lighter, fearing that the other party would crush it.
"That's not how it works."
He pressed his thumb, there was a soft "click" sound, and a cluster of orange fire burst out.
"Look, this is it."
The Taoist priest stared at the fire and remained silent for a long time.
The young apprentice also came closer, his honest face full of surprise: "It's really strange, it doesn't contain any spiritual power fluctuations!"
Shen Hui handed over the lighter, picked up the dead branches at his feet, and plucked the sweet potatoes buried in the fire.
The burnt incense mixed with the charcoal gas dispersed, and there was finally some warmth in the ruined temple.
He began to feel lucky again that he had used a lighter instead of a napkin. At least he could still eat warm food now, right?
The thin old Taoist took the lighter from his apprentice's hand and looked around, his fingertips glowing with a glistening green light:
"There is a trace of the aftertaste of heavenly thunder inside, and a little bit of earth evil spirit outside..."
He suddenly narrowed his eyes, "Brother, where did this thing come from?"
"A little trick passed down from our ancestors."
Shen Hui's expression remained unchanged as he pulled out two small sweet potatoes from the fire, feeling secretly despised in his heart.
The aftertaste of thunder from the sky and the essence of earth evil are nothing more than the piezoelectric ceramics and liquid butane in a lighter.
As a time traveler who hadn't eaten hot food for three days, he was only thinking about the sweet potatoes in his hand and had no time to dwell on these mysteries.
As for the two unknown Taoist priests in front of them... let alone wanting to see his lighter, even if they wanted to kill him as a monster, they had to wait for him to fill his stomach first.
Shen Hui used his sleeves to pick up a sweet potato, blew on it with his left and right hands, and quickly peeled off the scorched skin with his fingers.
There was some charcoal ash on the skin, but he didn't throw it away. He stuffed it into his mouth and chewed it carefully.
The sweet potato was not big, so he devoured it in just a few bites.
After swallowing the last bite of sweet potato, Shen Hui took the opportunity to glance at the two of them.
I saw the old Taoist priest with a thin face and a gray preaching robe that had been washed white. There was a slender wooden box tied to his back and wrapped with a cloth belt.
The young apprentice had a dark face and was carrying a rattan box half as tall as a man. There was a bell hanging on the corner of the box and an eye-catching red gourd.
Tsk!
This doesn’t look good!
Shen Hui smacked his teeth and thought to himself that these two people seemed quite popular in their words, but what about their outfits...
How can I put it, the appearance is indeed a bit fairy-like, but have you ever seen an expert wearing straw sandals? Still on such a cold day!
